item.title: NVIDIA DSX AI Factory Platform adds open‑source tools for reliable GPU‑Kubernetes clusters
item.description:
NVIDIA DSX AI Factory Platform adds open‑source tools for reliable GPU‑Kubernetes clusters

One underperforming GPU can slow an entire distributed training job, so measuring goodput – the volume of work successfully completed – is a more useful way to gauge cluster efficiency. NVIDIA’s DSX AI Factory Platform bundles the technologies needed to design, build, and operate efficient, resilient AI factories.

🔍 Overview

  • The platform’s open‑source software layer, NVIDIA DSX OS, provides tools for configuring, certifying, and maintaining the health of accelerated Kubernetes infrastructure.
  • It aims to keep every GPU, node, and network component in a ready state so that goodput remains high across large training jobs.

🛠️ Components

Component What it does
NVIDIA DSX OS Configures, certifies, and maintains accelerated Kubernetes clusters.
NVIDIA AI Cluster Runtime (AICR) Establishes a reproducible, version‑locked baseline for GPU‑optimized Kubernetes infrastructure; renders configuration recipes as bundles for existing deployment tools.
NVIDIA Cluster Readiness Engine (NVCRE) Validates cluster readiness for production workloads; tests GPUs, networking, and storage with AI workloads and diagnostics; records certification results and flags faulty nodes.
NVSentinel Monitors cluster health; publishes node conditions based on GPU, node, and network health; cordons or taints unhealthy nodes, drains workloads, remediates faults, and can trigger re‑validation with NVCRE before returning nodes to service.

All three projects are licensed under Apache 2.0 and welcome external contributions.

⚙️ How it works

  • AICR defines the cluster’s software baseline in version‑controlled files and renders them into artifacts that any deployment tool can apply.
  • Declarative templates detect configuration drift from manual changes and keep node configurations consistent after repairs.
  • Each recipe entry pins a component version, declares required healthy dependencies, and includes a healthCheckAsserts block that runs after installation.
  • The health assertions filter on the container waiting reason rather than the pod phase alone.
  • The bundle command produces ready‑to‑use artifacts: 
    1

    aicr bundle --recipe recipe.yaml --deployer argocd --output ./bundles
  • The --deployer flag accepts helm, argocd, argocd‑helm, flux, or helmfile, so the same validated recipe can become Argo CD Application manifests, Flux resources, a Helmfile release graph, or plain Helm commands.
  • Because the recipe is a file, standard version‑control workflows (history, code review, drift detection) manage the baseline.
  • Drift detection can be enforced as a CI gate: 
    1

    aicr diff --baseline ./golden.yaml --target cm://default/aicr-snapshot --fail-on-drift

📊 Measuring Efficiency

  • Goodput focuses on the actual work completed, highlighting the impact of any slow GPU on overall training performance.

🚀 Availability

  • The DSX OS, AICR, NVCRE, and NVSentinel projects are all open source under the Apache 2.0 license.
  • External contributions are encouraged, and the tools integrate with common GitOps deployment pipelines.

#NVIDIA #Kubernetes #AIInfrastructure #GPUClusters

Source: Configure, Certify, and Operate Kubernetes GPU Clusters with NVIDIA DSX OS | NVIDIA Technical Blog

item.title: Ai2 Replaces Priority-Based GPU Scheduling with Hierarchical Fair-Share Budgeting System
item.description:
Ai2 Replaces Priority-Based GPU Scheduling with Hierarchical Fair-Share Budgeting System

The AI Infrastructure team at Ai2 has updated its compute management strategy by replacing a legacy priority-based scheduler with a system featuring GPU time budgets, hierarchical fair-share allocation, and a time-slicing contract. This new approach shifts resource management from case-by-case operational tasks to a transparent administrative process designed to handle demand that consistently exceeds available capacity by 2-3x.

🔍 Overview

Ai2 manages thousands of NVIDIA H100, B200, and B300 GPUs organized in clusters ranging from 88 to 1024 units. These resources support approximately 150 internal researchers working on diverse AI domains, including:

  • Full model flow for LLM and VLM training.
  • Robotics reinforcement learning (RL) simulation. 0* Post-training for scientific agentic use cases.

🧩 How it works

The new system is built on a hierarchy of needs designed to optimize distributed training workloads. Instead of solving a manual “knapsack problem” to fit research needs into a static schedule, leadership now allocates portions of GPU time in advance, allowing them to fund research efforts based on projected impact.

Level Component Description
Capstone Utilization The fraction of GPU capacity used over the lifetime of a workload.
Level 3 Impact How often the most valuable workloads are chosen to receive resources.
Level 2 Occupancy The fraction of available time assigned to a specific workload.
Foundation Availability How often the hardware is healthy and ready for work.

⚙️ Key details

The transition addresses several critical inefficiencies identified in the previous priority-based model:

  • Priority Inflation: Historically, 100% of scheduled workloads eventually used “HIGH” priority, starving lower-priority levels of GPU time.
  • GPU Squatting: Users previously parked “no-op” workloads to maintain access to resources, preventing others from launching real-time debugging tasks.
  • Maintenance Overhead: Because preemptability was optional, engineers spent significant time negotiating shutdowns for hardware maintenance.
  • Seasonality Issues: Previous attempts to assign GPU monopolies to specific teams caused resources to sit idle during natural lulls in research cycles.

💡 Why it matters

By moving to a time-budgeting model, Ai2 enables leadership to think like investors. Since research demand cannot be forecast with total precision due to the nature of novel science, the institute now decides how to fund research efforts before the workloads even exist. This ensures that every available GPU hour is allocated based on strategy rather than individual competition for scarce resources.

#AIinfrastructure #GPUclusters #Ai2 #MachineLearning #DistributedTraining

Source: Impactful scheduling for GPU clusters
